samples.text:
The chart show the main ways which people in four cities use to go to their work.

In Northport, the car is the most common method with 62%. Public transport is 20%, walking is 12% and cycling is only 6%, which is the lowest number in the chart. In Arden the car is also the most popular, 45% of workers use it. Then there is public transport with 25%, cycling with 20% and walking with 10%.

However, Kelby and Southam are different. In Kelby the public transport is most popular with 48% and the car is only 30%. Cycling and walking are 12% and 10%. In Southam, cycling is the main method, because 45% of the workers are cycling to work. Public transport is 22%, car is 18% and walking is 15%.

Overall, the car is popular in Northport and Arden, but in Kelby people prefer public transport and in Southam they prefer bicycle. Walking was not very popular in any of the city.
samples.why: All figures accurate · overview basic and only at the end · city-by-city listing with mechanical linking · repetitive vocabulary · several article, agreement and tense errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares the proportions of workers in four cities who used the car, public transport, cycling or walking as their main way of commuting.

Overall, the dominant form of transport varied from city to city. Driving was the most common choice in Northport and Arden, whereas public transport and cycling were the most popular in Kelby and Southam respectively. Walking, by comparison, was a minor option everywhere.

Northport had the highest reliance on cars, with 62% of workers driving to work, followed by public transport at 20%. Only 6% of commuters there cycled, the lowest figure for any method in the four city. Arden showed a similar but less extreme pattern: 45% travelled by car, while a quarter used public transport and a further 20% cycled.

In Kelby, by contrast, nearly half of the workforce (48%) took public transport, compared with 30% who drove. Southam was notable for its cyclists, who made up 45% of commuters, while cars accounted for only 18%, the smallest share in any of the cities. Walking was consistently low, ranging between 10% and 15%, with the highest proportion recorded in Southam.
samples.why: Clear overview of each city's dominant mode · key features well highlighted and compared · logical organisation with a range of linkers · good collocations · mostly error-free with one minor slip.

samples.text:
The chart illustrates how commuters in four cities, Northport, Kelby, Arden and Southam, chose to travel to work, broken down into four modes of transport.

What stands out is that each city had a distinctive commuting profile. Cars were the principal means of travel in Northport and Arden, but public transport led in Kelby and cycling in Southam. Walking, meanwhile, played a relatively small role in all four cities.

Northport was by far the most car-dependent city, with 62% of its workers driving, roughly three times the proportion using public transport (20%). Cycling was almost negligible there, at just 6%. Arden also favoured the car, though less heavily, at 45%, and it had a more even spread across the other modes, with 25% using public transport and 20% cycling.

Kelby and Southam presented a sharp contrast. In Kelby, public transport was the choice of 48% of commuters, well ahead of the car at 30%, while in Southam cycling accounted for 45%, making driving (18%) a relatively minor option. Walking figures were broadly similar throughout, ranging from 10% in Kelby and Arden to 15% in Southam.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected · clear, well-placed overview · figures used selectively to compare cities · cohesion managed well · wide, precise vocabulary · varied, error-free structures.
